actions.reason: K6_C0001 has an interpretable biological identity (proliferation up-regulation with oxidative-phosphorylation/metabolic down-regulation, and uniform PBRM1 mutation surviving multiplicity control), but identity alone does not establish independent membership. The set-level native-geometry report shows essentially no within-versus-rest distinction (silhouettes near zero, marginally reversed in CT/WSI/WXS), and the pair-level boundary against K6_C0004 is unexpressed in CT, RNA, and WSI with separation confined to WXS alone. No decision-relevant membership or boundary evidence positively supports treating the current membership as an independent unit, so retention is not justified.

K6_C0002 has an interpretable biological identity (coordinated immune/interferon down-regulation with oxidative-phosphorylation and fatty-acid metabolism up-regulation), but identity alone does not establish independent membership. The set-level native-geometry report shows only modest positive silhouettes, and the pair-level boundary against K6_C0003 is essentially unexpressed in fused geometry (boundary silhouette ~0.0004, within-set and between-set affinities nearly identical) with only small native-geometry separation. The union is single-cluster dominated, which is not evidence against merge but also not positive support for the current boundary. No evidence positively supports treating the current membership as an independent unit, so retention is not justified.

K6_C0003 has an interpretable biological identity (coordinated immune/interferon up-regulation with EMT/myogenesis down-regulation), but identity alone does not establish independent membership. The set-level native-geometry report shows essentially no within-versus-rest distinction (silhouettes near zero, marginally reversed in CT/WSI), the boundary against K6_C0002 is essentially unexpressed in fused geometry, and the boundary against K6_C0006 is only modestly expressed with the strongest separation confined to WXS. No evidence positively supports treating the current membership as an independent unit, so retention is not justified.

K6_C0004 has an interpretable biological identity (immune/interferon and proliferation down-regulation with TGF-beta up-regulation), but identity alone does not establish independent membership. The set-level native-geometry report shows essentially no within-versus-rest distinction (silhouettes near zero, negative in WSI), the boundary against K6_C0001 is unexpressed in CT, RNA, and WSI, and the boundary against K6_C0006 is likewise unexpressed in CT, RNA, and WSI with separation confined to WXS. The WXS mutation contrast yields no adjusted driver-level signal. No evidence positively supports treating the current membership as an independent unit, so retention is not justified.

K6_C0005 has an interpretable biological identity: coordinated immune/interferon up-regulation with MYC-target, ROS, and DNA-repair programs, plus a BAP1-enriched driver profile (9/17 versus 4/86; OR 23.06) that survives driver-panel and global multiplicity control. Unlike the other candidates, its set-level native-geometry report shows positive silhouettes in all four modalities with within-set distances consistently smaller than between-set distances, providing direct membership-representation support for treating the current membership as a separately represented unit. No material direct counterevidence to this membership representation was returned, so retention for downstream stability aggregation is justified.

K6_C0006 has an interpretable biological identity (EMT/stromal up-regulation with oxidative-phosphorylation and immune/interferon down-regulation), but identity alone does not establish independent membership. The set-level native-geometry report shows essentially no within-versus-rest distinction (silhouettes near zero, marginally reversed in CT/WSI/WXS), the boundary against K6_C0003 is only modestly expressed with the strongest separation confined to WXS, and the boundary against K6_C0004 is unexpressed in CT, RNA, and WSI. No evidence positively supports treating the current membership as an independent unit, so retention is not justified.
